steps.content: Thunder rumbles within the dark clouds. Rain pours over Eastside, sending the city into a dreary haze.

Police lights flicker beneath the shadow of the trees before the manor. Reporters have completely surrounded the place, cameras in hand. At the center of it all, a middle-aged maid is being escorted into a police car.
Through the jostling crowd, you catch the eye of a frazzled-looking sheriff.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: You're late, Chief. The maid's already confessed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I read the report on the way. I'm only here to confirm the situation. This makes three cases now, doesn't it?

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: That's correct... Shipping tycoon Porto, banker Leighton, and now young Humbert. All of them died under bizarre circumstances, yet in each case, someone came forward immediately with a confession.

Strange cases have been cropping up across Eastside recently. Last month, shipping tycoon Porto suffered brain death due to a malfunctioning nutrition pod, and the resuscitation failed. Banker Leighton, on the other hand, died of a heart attack after mistakenly ingesting NSAIDs.
As for this case, which occurred early this morning, the Humbert estate owner's only son was found dead in his bathroom. A garter stocking was pulled tight around his neck.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The ones who confessed... do they all have grudges against the victims?

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Porto's gardener had a daughter who was used as a test subject for his nutrition pods. Leighton's chauffeur had a son who was driven to jump off a building over debt. As for today's case...

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Years ago, young Humbert drove after drinking and killed a college freshman in a hit-and-run. Due to damaged surveillance footage and the reported vehicle being stolen, the police never pressed charges.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And the victim was that maid's only daughter.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Precisely. She confessed to the crime without hesitation. Strangely enough, though, she refuses to reveal how she did it, no matter what we ask.
Technically speaking, none of these cases fall under MBCC jurisdiction, but...

Something feels off. The victims in all these cases were wealthy elites with long histories of committing vile acts, none of which were ever brought to justice. The perpetrators were all people they had wronged, and somehow, each one devised an incredibly sophisticated plan to bypass security and got close to their targets...
As if they were following a <color=#fb9259>script</color> someone wrote for them.

You step into the bathroom. It seems there should be crystal chandeliers hanging from each corner of the ceiling, but right now, one lies shattered, and another spot is empty. Freshly starched shirts and aprons are scattered across the floor along with some undergarments.
Honestly, at first glance, this could easily pass for the scene of an accident. But then, you catch a faint glint in your peripheral vision as you examine the area once more.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is...
[Scene Change: A Room, Night]

Click. A woman flicks on an old floor lamp as she enters, casting a dim, amber glow across the room. The air carries the scent of aged paper, beeswax, and the faintest fragrance of bitter orange flower.

Strange collectibles can be found on the desk—butterfly specimens, acorns, and several worn dice. A well-thumbed book bound in dark red leather lies facing down. A slender hand picks it up, fingertips trailing across the words on its pages.
A chandelier, fishing lines, and a perfectly timed accident... Not a bad piece of work, wouldn't you say?
The wind stirs the curtains. An uninvited shadow appears in the room.

This, however, doesn't surprise her. She slowly closes the book and returns it to the shelf, then reaches for a crystal wine glass. She then leisurely pours wine into the empty glass, all while smiling in the direction of the shadow.
A visit at this hour... Did you come to share a drink with me before bed? My dear detective, ${PlayerName}.

Looks like there's no point in hiding anymore. You step out from the shadows and seize her slender, delicate wrist in one swift motion. Since she is holding the glass with that hand, the wine spills, just as expected.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This time, we'll be having a chat at the Bureau, <color=#fb9259>Clementine</color>.

In the interrogation room, Clementine sits with perfect composure, not showing even the slightest hint of discomfort. Two cups of hot tea have been set on the table between you. Through the rising steam, a faint smile plays on her lips.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It's been a while, ${PlayerName}. You look terrible. Have you not been sleeping well?

options: You have no clue how much time I spent looking for you.

choices.text: You have no clue how much time I spent looking for you.

steps.content: The last reported sighting of her came from the surveillance team stationed outside Clementine's home. She vanished within the burning Mania, and shortly after, news of the Redwood arsonist's death broke out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After we parted that day, Banbury Manor caught fire under unknown circumstances. Charles Banbury, the "Carl" from your book, was confirmed dead in the flames.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Redwood fire case was reopened, and the investigation resumed. The Public Security Bureau followed the trail and uncovered numerous old cases that had been suppressed in the same way. I promised you I would see the investigation through to the end, that I would deliver justice for everyone...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But you broke your promise.

You've spent so long worrying about her. This reunion really should be a touching one, but seeing her sit across from you now, acting as though nothing happened at all, you can't help but feel extremely annoyed.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now, now, there's no need to look so stern. Why don't we talk about something more interesting?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The only thing I'm interested in right now is the final step of your vengeance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How did you kill Carl, and how did you escape the fire? What have you been doing all this time you've been missing?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hehe... What are you talking about? Didn't the authorities already state that it was an <color=#fb9259>accident</color>?

She clearly has no intention of telling you what really happened that day—not how she dealt with the assassin, how she breached the layers of security to reach Carl's residence, how she ended his life...
Nor how she vanished in the sea of flames, letting the fire consume every trace of evidence.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So even you didn't expect to make it out of that "accident" alive?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Yup, it was just a stroke of luck. An old friend came to my rescue, so I barely made it out. I just wanted to give myself a little vacation for once to rest and recover, since I'm always being hounded by deadlines. That's not so strange, is it?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You should try to relax every now and then too. Investigating cases can be interesting, but don't let it become an obsession.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's ironic, coming from someone who always writes protagonists that eagerly throw themselves into trouble to solve other people's problems.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: True. And in the world of stories, good people are always rewarded. You're much like one of those lucky protagonists who were blessed by fate.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll have you know that there was no such thing as fate or good luck. Accidental fires are dangerous, and that artificial rainfall cost me three months' worth of salary.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm putting this on your tab. Don't even think about running off before you've paid me back.
Clementine looks both surprised and amused. She raises her teacup and gently clinks it against yours.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Thank you, ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I knew you're one to keep your word. I trusted that... Even if I'm not around, you'd still honor our agreement and see the investigation through to the end.
She leans forward, her gaze clear and filled with genuine curiosity.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But I'm still curious about something, Chief. How did you find me?
test
test
test
test
test
test

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: These cases weren't originally under my jurisdiction, especially since all the suspects seemed to have a death wish. They all confessed to their crimes on the spot.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If that's the case, the cases should have been closed right then and there.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You seem to have forgotten that I've been a devoted reader of yours for quite some time now. The medical malpractice case, the drug poisoning case, and now this stocking murder case... Shouldn't they all seem rather familiar to you?
You flip through the case files and stop at a photo of the crime scene from the stocking murder case.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Here—there's a thin fishing line strung between the chandelier hook and the ventilation window handle.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Those lights may look nice, but they're notoriously unreliable. If one breaks, another's bound to follow. When someone finishes using the restroom and opens the window to air it out, the stocking would come falling down along with the fishing line.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Most people would assume the clothesline goes on empty hooks, but what if it was attached to that light instead? What if that light was only held to the ceiling by that single rope?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When the victim stood up to open the window, the rope went slack. The chandelier came crashing down, its falling weight yanked the stocking upward, and then—
You mimic the motion of a neck snapping.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The method is identical to the one in that old book on your desk, no?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I joked about how some of the methods in your books were practically a how-to guide for criminals, that you've probably had a hand in Eastside's rising crime rate... but I never imagined you'd actually get directly involved in helping them.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It seems you've been quite devoted to your research. To think you've even read my earliest work.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But... what if they're simply a fan of mine who used a method I'd written about? Would that make it my responsibility still?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If that were all, I probably wouldn't have suspected you so quickly.
You spread out the case files. Red circles mark numerous sections across the pages, with lines connecting clue to clue, mapping out a series of crimes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Every suspect in these cases is an ordinary citizen from the lower class. At first glance, they appear to have no connection to the victims, but upon investigation, it turns out they'd all been wronged by the deceased. After exhausting every legal avenue with nowhere to turn, they resorted to murder.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even so, their targets were heavily protected. Given these suspects' limited means, they should never have been able to get past those defenses...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...But they succeeded anyway. I've met with them, and nearly every single one of them used methods far beyond their own capabilities. They carried out their vengeance with remarkable sophistication.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The timeline starts shortly after you disappeared and runs up until last week. What made them all choose to act within this specific window? Can that really be a coincidence?
You press Clementine, but she remains unfazed.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It's just a coincidence, of course. There wouldn't have been enough time. Even I need considerable effort to craft such sophisticated crimes in my novels.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But if you insist on pinning this on me...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Perhaps Redwood gave them hope. They realized that injustice is only addressed when it becomes a scandal. Taking such desperate measures isn't so strange given their circumstances, wouldn't you say?
For a fleeting moment, you catch what looks like a sly glint in Clementine's eye. However, in the next instant, her expression returns to one of detached indifference.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Why couldn't it be a miracle of love? Maybe that gave them the power to achieve vengeance against all odds?

options: Alright then, is this also a coincidence?

choices.text: Alright then, is this also a coincidence?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You can dismiss everything I've said so far as speculation, but how do you explain this?
You pull out a slightly creased card and hold it over the teacup on the table. After a moment, a string of numbers appears on its surface.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The maid had a card sewn into her collar. If it hadn't been exposed to the steam, no one would have ever found this hidden message.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Once is a coincidence. Twice, however, is proof.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Blank cards like this were found at every crime scene. The method used to reveal them appeared in your novels, and they all contain your contact information. That's when I knew for certain that you're alive, and that you're the one orchestrating these three cases, Clementine.
The room falls silent.
After a long pause, soft applause begins ringing.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You're as sharp as ever.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Through observing the scene alone, you managed to reconstruct the methods used. Most importantly, you found decisive evidence, leaving the mastermind with no room for denial.
Her cavalier attitude irritates you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why use this method to help people get vengeance? I don't understand, there should be better methods available.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll see Carl's case through to the end, and I won't give up on any of these either. Even if they're not related to Mania, I can still help investigate and vindicate these injustices.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why do you find it necessary to force yourself, and all those other victims, down the path of crime? I—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Pray tell, then, Chief—what exactly can you do?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You might be able to help them track down the criminals and expose the crimes. But you know as well as I do that those bastards, who deserve the death penalty, will keep getting shielded by their connections and walk away with a slap on the wrist.
Her smile vanishes completely in the face of your questioning. The warm atmosphere of your reunion dissipates in an instant, as if it had never existed at all.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Public opinion can be manipulated. The truth can be buried. And even if a conviction is secured... retribution would fall on those poor souls who dared to resist, long before the perpetrator walks free.
She leans back in her chair and tilts her head up slightly. The steam clears, revealing a hollow, emotionless gaze.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: DisCity is vast, and there are more souls holding grievances than anyone can count. Not everyone can make it to your office door, much less survive long enough to see justice done.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The Redwood case alone took ten years. How many decades can ordinary people afford to lose?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Besides... think about our current situation. You're not just here to catch up with me, are you? Someone ordered you to find Carl's killer. Oh, and to apprehend the mastermind behind those three cases.
You're left speechless. Everything she said is true.
Seeing this, Clementine's voice softens, regaining its gentle warmth.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I'm sorry. I didn't say all that to condemn you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Quite the contrary, in fact. I very much admire your sincerity and integrity. You possess something beautiful—something I stopped believing I'd ever see again long ago... Your very existence brings hope to those still struggling in the dark.
Clementine reaches out, her fingertips brushing across your cheek tenderly.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But not everyone seeks the light.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That's just how this world is. There are good people like you who charge ahead stubbornly, no matter how battered and bruised you get... and then there are utterly irredeemable bastards like Carl.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But most ordinary people are caught in between. They're too kind to avoid being trampled, but too powerless to fight back.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: There are people you and the law cannot help... so I'll help them instead.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hatred can only be dispelled by blood. Just passing judgment on the villains isn't enough, considering how much they've lost.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Have you thought about the consequences?! This is nothing more than mutual destruction! Their lives will be completely ruined afterward—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Their lives were already ruined.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: After everything they've been through, do you really think they can just go on with life as if nothing had happened?
Clementine's voice sounds distant. She's talking about others, but you hear something deeper in her words—a profound grief.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: They have nothing left but hatred and rage.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Those who come to me are all like that. That's why they're willing to step into my stories, take up the blade, and become its protagonist.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: For them... this is the only way to live.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...And then what happens?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hm?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Criminals need to serve their time and atone, but life goes on. What happens after they're released? How are they supposed to live the rest of their lives?
"What choices will they have then?" The words almost slip out, but you stop yourself.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What happens after? The fact that even an outsider like you, Chief, can feel the anguish of the characters in this story... I think that shows it has served its purpose well enough.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As for me...
Clementine's smile turns distant. She's sitting right across from you, yet she feels impossibly far away.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Imprisonment, punishment, whatever it is, go ahead and follow your procedures. Don't worry. I knew the risks when I made my bet.
[End of Interrogation - Scene Change]
The interrogation ends. Clementine admitted to assisting the suspects in all three cases, yet you feel no satisfaction whatsoever.
You open the comms.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, did the interrogation go smoothly? You look troubled.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The interrogation went about as I expected. Clementine is willing to accept the consequences, but she's not truly repentant. Given her current state, we can't let her leave the Bureau, much less hand her over to the Public Security Bureau.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nightingale, keep a close eye on Clementine's condition. Pay special attention to anyone she might be in contact with, and monitor her behavior when she interacts with the other Sinners.
After giving Nightingale instructions, you sit alone in your office, anxiety still gnawing at you. You open the recording again—the one you've listened to countless times already.
Ma'am, you've been drawing quite a bit of attention lately. This doesn't seem like your usual approach.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You mean before I "died"?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Give me a little more time. A sudden death takes its toll, even a staged one.
Time... of course. We've always valued talented partners, but we also value those who know when to exercise restraint. That is the foundation of a lasting partnership.
We simply expect satisfactory results. Don't keep <color=#fb9259>her</color> waiting too long.
You've lost count of how many times you've listened to this conversation, yet some of the words and tones in it still leave you deeply unsettled.

The person in the recording must be the old friend Clementine mentioned—<color=#fb9259>the Sillage Society</color>, an organization that operates in the shadows of the city-state. They were the ones who gave Clementine Mania, the power to exact her revenge, and now they're inviting her to plunge into the abyss alongside them.
The society is trying to recruit Clementine, yet she's hesitating for once.

She vanished, only to reappear out of nowhere, and then she used these acts of revenge as a message to show that she's still alive. But why? Is it a cry for help? Or is she really just doing what she claims... enacting justice in her own way?
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Their lives were already ruined.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: They have nothing left but hatred and rage.
[End of Flashback]
Clementine's novels are still on your desk. Both the popular and obscure ones. Were the people in her stories really just characters meant to serve a tale of vengeance?
[Flash portraits of the train passengers from the main story]

You turn to the case file at your side. The victim list for the Redwood arson is painted in stark red, while the survivor column holds only a handful of names. And even those were buried in WhiteSands years ago, leaving Clementine as the only one left.
Perhaps the person whose life was destroyed, who has nothing left but hatred and rage... is Clementine herself.
You can't let her fall to the darkness. You have to do something.
You can only hope it's not too late.
